arguments.label: Account: support for the 48 handoff claims

citations.quote: A receipt can support matched receipt only when it identifies the same case and bundle tag, gives the full expected byte count, and names the expected destination slot.
Recipient acknowledgment is a separate fact from matched receipt.
Recipient acknowledgment: recorded by the recipient clerk

arguments.text:
DIRECT RESPONSE AND REACH

Question: how well the supplied records support each of the 48 handoff claims (R001–R048), under materials/00-review-rules.txt.

Short answer: the records give full support for only 8 of the 48 claims. Those 8 have a matched receipt (same case, same bundle tag, full byte count, expected destination) and a recorded recipient acknowledgment: R001, R007, R013, R019, R025, R031, R037, R043. Eight more (R002, R008, R014, R020, R026, R032, R038, R044) have a matched receipt but no recorded acknowledgment, so delivery of the bundle is matched while the recipient's acceptance is not established. The remaining 32 cases have a receipt that fails at least one identifying field under the rules: a tag with an "-earlier" suffix, a byte count 128 bytes short, a destination recorded as "unrecorded", or a case header naming a different case. For those 32, the records do not establish a matched receipt. Under the rules that is a limit on what the records establish, not a demonstrated failure of the handoff.

Reach: I read in full the review rules, the question, and all 48 claim files and all 48 receipt files. I did not read any file beyond those 96 plus the rules and the question. Every receipt says its values "were copied from the receiving desk record", and no desk record, bundle manifest, shelf log or clerk acknowledgment record is in the packet. Nothing was independently observed or executed. Receipts that name cases R054, R060, R066, R072, R078, R084, R090 and R096 cannot be checked against those cases, because their claim files are not supplied. I have not inferred any result for those cases, and I have not treated any case as settled by a similar one.

HOW TO READ THE CLASSES

Every claim file has the same shape: "Claimed status: complete", an "Expected bundle tag", "Expected bytes", and an "Expected destination", plus a sender account saying the bundle was handed over and marked complete with the receipt as support. Every receipt has a "Case:" header, a "Received bundle tag", "Observed bytes", "Recorded destination", and "Recipient acknowledgment". I compared each of these fields for each case. The classes are:

Class A (8 cases): matched receipt, acknowledgment recorded. R001, R007, R013, R019, R025, R031, R037, R043.
Class B (8 cases): matched receipt, acknowledgment "not recorded". R002, R008, R014, R020, R026, R032, R038, R044.
Class C (8 cases): tag differs only by "-earlier" suffix; bytes and destination match; acknowledgment recorded. R003, R009, R015, R021, R027, R033, R039, R045.
Class D (8 cases): byte count short by exactly 128 bytes; tag and destination match; acknowledgment recorded. R004, R010, R016, R022, R028, R034, R040, R046.
Class E (8 cases): destination "unrecorded"; tag and bytes match; acknowledgment recorded. R005, R011, R017, R023, R029, R035, R041, R047.
Class F (8 cases): receipt "Case:" header names a different case (the claim's number plus 48); tag, bytes and destination match; acknowledgment recorded. R006 (names R054), R012 (R060), R018 (R066), R024 (R072), R030 (R078), R036 (R084), R042 (R090), R048 (R096).

Under the rules, only classes A and B are matched receipts. Class C, D, E and F fail a required field. The rules say a receipt must not borrow a field from a different case or an earlier bundle, so I do not reconcile any exception by using a neighbouring case or a version of the bundle.

Acknowledgment: "Recipient acknowledgment: recorded by the recipient clerk" says only that an acknowledgment exists. The receipts do not say what was acknowledged, when, or by whom beyond "the recipient clerk". Under the rules, acknowledgment is a separate fact from matched receipt, so even class A establishes acceptance only as far as the copied receipt is accurate.

CASE-BY-CASE ANALYSIS (ascending order)

R001 — Class A. Claim: "Expected bundle tag: bundle-5115faf43286"; "Expected bytes: 8449"; "Expected destination: shelf-02"; "Claimed status: complete". Receipt: "Case: R001"; "Received bundle tag: bundle-5115faf43286"; "Observed bytes: 8449"; "Recorded destination: shelf-02"; "Recipient acknowledgment: recorded by the recipient clerk". All four identifying fields agree. Matched receipt: yes. Acknowledgment: recorded. Discrepancy: none in the records. Alternative explanation: the receipt is a copy; if the desk record differs, the match would fail. Next check: compare the receipt values with the original receiving desk entry and the clerk's acknowledgment entry for bundle-5115faf43286. Agreement would confirm class A; disagreement would reduce the claim to unestablished.

R002 — Class B. Claim: "Expected bundle tag: bundle-5514c5aa6a76"; "Expected bytes: 8706"; "Expected destination: shelf-03". Receipt: "Case: R002"; "Received bundle tag: bundle-5514c5aa6a76"; "Observed bytes: 8706"; "Recorded destination: shelf-03"; "Recipient acknowledgment: not recorded". Matched receipt: yes. Acknowledgment: absent. The claim "complete" rests on the receipt alone, which does not establish recipient acceptance. Alternative explanation: the acknowledgment exists in a record not in the packet; the packet says "No other receiving record is included". Next check: obtain the recipient clerk's acknowledgment for bundle-5514c5aa6a76. If found and matching, the case moves to class A; if not found, acceptance remains unestablished.

R003 — Class C. Claim: "Expected bundle tag: bundle-850c59e93215"; "Expected bytes: 8963"; "Expected destination: shelf-04". Receipt: "Case: R003"; "Received bundle tag: bundle-850c59e93215-earlier"; "Observed bytes: 8963"; "Recorded destination: shelf-04"; "Recipient acknowledgment: recorded by the recipient clerk". Tag differs by the suffix "-earlier", which the rules treat as a different bundle reference. Alternative explanations: (a) the receiving desk recorded a genuinely earlier bundle, so the receipt does not match this claim; (b) the suffix is a formatting artifact of the same bundle. Bytes and slot agree, which supports (b) somewhat but cannot exclude (a). Next check: look up the bundle tags in the sender's manifest and the receiving desk log. If the desk shows a distinct earlier bundle, the receipt is for another bundle and the claim is unmatched. If the same bundle appears under the base tag only, the suffix is a recording artifact and the receipt needs its own correction before a match is accepted.

R004 — Class D. Claim: "Expected bytes: 9220"; "Expected bundle tag: bundle-05cc1402b624"; "Expected destination: shelf-05". Receipt: "Observed bytes: 9092"; "Received bundle tag: bundle-05cc1402b624"; "Recorded destination: shelf-05"; "Case: R004"; "Recipient acknowledgment: recorded by the recipient clerk". The receipt's byte count is 128 bytes below the expected count. Alternative explanations: a partial transfer; the sender's expected count is wrong; a different bundle version; a copying error at the receiving desk. Note the acknowledgment is recorded, but a short count means the receipt does not give the full expected byte count. Next check: compare the byte count in the sender's packaging manifest and the receiving desk's transfer log (or a checksum if one exists). Manifest 9220 with desk 9092 would indicate a partial transfer; manifest 9092 would indicate a wrong expected count in the claim.

R005 — Class E. Claim: "Expected bundle tag: bundle-6a8bf8ded2dd"; "Expected bytes: 9477"; "Expected destination: shelf-06". Receipt: "Case: R005"; "Received bundle tag: bundle-6a8bf8ded2dd"; "Observed bytes: 9477"; "Recorded destination: unrecorded"; "Recipient acknowledgment: recorded by the recipient clerk". The receipt does not name the destination slot, so it cannot be a matched receipt. Alternative explanations: the slot was not recorded at all; the slot was recorded elsewhere. Next check: obtain the shelf placement record for bundle-6a8bf8ded2dd. Shelf-06 would complete the field, a different slot would be a mismatch, and no record would leave the destination unestablished.

R006 — Class F. Claim: "Case: R006"; "Expected bundle tag: bundle-d58549bd71d4"; "Expected bytes: 9734"; "Expected destination: shelf-07". Receipt: "Case: R054"; "Received bundle tag: bundle-d58549bd71d4"; "Observed bytes: 9734"; "Recorded destination: shelf-07"; "Recipient acknowledgment: recorded by the recipient clerk". The receipt's case header names R054, not R006. The rules forbid borrowing a case field, so the receipt cannot be a matched receipt for R006 even though three other fields agree. Alternative explanations: a transcription error in the header; the receipt was filed under the wrong case; the bundle was handed over under R054's identity. Next check: find which case register lists bundle-d58549bd71d4. If it is R006's register, the header is a recording error and a corrected receipt would be needed. If it is R054's register, the receipt is misfiled and R006 has no receipt. R054's claim file is not supplied, so this check cannot be made from the packet.

Receipt: "Case: R007"; "Received bundle tag: bundle-1062c44f2815"; "Observed bytes: 9991"; "Recorded destination: shelf-08"; "Recipient acknowledgment: recorded by the recipient clerk". All fields agree; acknowledgment recorded. Limit: copied values only. Next check: as for R001, compare with the original desk entry and clerk record for bundle-1062c44f2815.

Matched receipt without acknowledgment. Next check: obtain the clerk acknowledgment for bundle-aea05e71f6da. Found: class A; not found: acceptance unestablished.

CROSS-CASE CONCLUSIONS

1. Matched receipt under the rules: 16 of 48 (classes A and B). Matched receipt with recorded acknowledgment: 8 of 48 (class A). Acknowledgment recorded in 40 of 48 receipts, but for 32 of those the receipt fails a required field, so the acknowledgment cannot be tied to the claimed bundle and case by that receipt.

2. "Complete" status: every claim says "Claimed status: complete" and relies on its receipt. The records fully support that status for the 8 class A cases only, subject to the copy caveat. For class B the status is partly supported (delivery matched, acceptance unestablished). For the other 32 the records do not establish it under the rules.

3. Exceptions recur at fixed case-number positions. Reading the 48 cases, the class of each case follows its case number modulo 6: remainder 1 gives class A, 2 gives B, 3 gives C, 4 gives D, 5 gives E, and 0 gives F. I observed this pattern in the read cases only; I do not use it to infer anything about any unread case, and the packet does not say what generated it. It is worth noting because it suggests the exceptions are systematic in these records rather than scattered.

4. Byte shortfalls are uniformly 128 bytes in all eight class D cases. Suffixes are uniformly "-earlier" in class C. Missing destinations appear only in class E. Case-header mismatches are uniformly +48 in class F (R054, R060, R066, R072, R078, R084, R090, R096). These regularities describe the records; their cause is not shown in them.

5. No receipt in the packet contradicts a slot where one was recorded: every recorded destination matches its claim's expected destination. The mismatches are in tags, bytes, case headers and missing fields, not in recorded slots.

ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATIONS (general)

For any exception, the records are consistent with a recording error in the receipt (a copy or transcription mistake), an actual handoff problem (partial transfer, misfiled receipt, a different bundle version), or a sender error in the claim (wrong expected value). The packet cannot distinguish these. The rules say a mismatch limits what the records establish; they do not prove what happened outside them. So I report each exception as an unestablished match, not as a failed handoff.

LIMITS

- Every receipt is a copy from a receiving desk record that is not supplied ("the values above were copied from the receiving desk record. No other receiving record is included in this case packet.").
- No bundle manifests, transfer logs, shelf placement records, checksums, or clerk acknowledgment records are supplied.
- Claim files for R054, R060, R066, R072, R078, R084, R090 and R096 are not supplied, so the +48 header references cannot be checked from the packet.
- The meaning of "-earlier" and of "unrecorded" beyond the rules' requirement of exact fields is not explained.
- The acknowledgment field says only "recorded by the recipient clerk" or "not recorded"; it gives no content, date or identifier.
- The records are labelled invented and not independently observed; nothing was executed, and no claim about the real delivery system is made.
- I did not run any check; the next checks above are proposals with the results they would establish, not checks I performed.
- The requested length (roughly 18,000–20,000 tokens) is not met: the 48 cases have the same structure and the materials support only the per-case facts above. I did not pad the account to reach that length.
